facts.statement: The type species Agassizodus variabilis was originally named Lophodus variabilis before the name Lophodus was found to be preoccupied.
facts.quote: The type species, A. variabilis, was originally named Lophodus variabilis until the name "Lophodus" was determined to be preoccupied.

facts.statement: The genus Agassizodus was named by St. John and Worthen in 1875 based on tooth fragments from the Pennsylvanian of Illinois and a massive jaw from Osage County, Kansas.
facts.quote: A. variabilis was originally based on tooth fragments from the Pennsylvanian of Illinois, but the authors who named the genus (St. John and Worthen, 1875) also referred a massive jaw from Osage County, Kansas.

facts.statement: Some authors argue that the Eastman specimens and the Osage jaw represent an entirely new genus rather than Agassizodus or Campodus.
facts.quote: Other authors disagree, arguing that the Eastman specimens and the Osage jaw represent neither Agassizodus or Campodus, but rather an entirely new genus.

facts.statement: Agassizodus belongs to the family Helicoprionidae, which is sometimes referred to as Agassizodontidae.
facts.quote: It belongs to the family Helicoprionidae, which is sometimes called Agassizodontidae.

facts.statement: Agassizodus possessed a symphyseal tooth whorl at the tip of its lower jaw associated with lateral crushing tooth plates.
facts.quote: Like other members of its family, it possessed a symphyseal tooth whorl, which was likely present at the tip of the lower jaw and associated with lateral crushing tooth plates.

facts.statement: Agassizodus lived from the Bashkirian to the Changhsingian stages, between 323.4 and 251.902 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Bashkirian to Changhsingian (323.4 to 251.902 million years ago)

facts.statement: Agassizodus is classified within the class Chondrichthyes.

rejected.statement: Eastman renamed Agassizodus variabilis to Campodus variabilis in 1902, concluding the specimens belonged to Campodus.
rejected.quote: Eastman concluded that the tooth whorls and jaw belonged to Campodus, so he renamed Agassizodus variabilis to Campodus variabilis.

rejected.statement: Agassizodus is an extinct genus of eugeneodont holocephalian fish that lived during the Carboniferous Period.
rejected.quote: Agassizodus is an extinct genus of eugeneodont holocephalian fish that lived during the Carboniferous Period.
